newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - BT shares may go to 445p then 490p.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - BT shares may go to 445p then 490p.

text.p: DAY'S RANGE * SUPPORT * RESTNCE* MA-25 * MA-200
Telecommunications * * * *
+ BT shares are capable of climbing up to the 435p-445p area near-term and after that a move to 490p may be possible, technical analysts said.
+ Breakout from a double-bottom pattern on a weekly chart of BT in November 1996 was bullish for the shares stock although the price-relative chart has so far failed to confirm this.
Shares in British Telecommunications have the potential to creep up towards the 435p-445p area, technical analysts said.
Provided bullish market conditions persist after that target has been met, a move to 490p may then be possible, they added.

"The shares have broken out of small base pattern (thereby) sweeping aside old resistance at 420p and are now ready to test their peak of 1993," said Richard Marshall, a director at Investment Research of Cambridge Ltd.
Calculations from the base pattern of December to January suggest the shares are close to ending their initial run up.
In that basing phase, BT shares traded from 390p to 405p.
By 1310 GMT, BT shares were up 6-1/2p to 427p.
"The chart signals are not clear (as to the pace of any further rises) from here," said Marshall.
Nick Glydon, technical analyst at Robert Fleming Securities, doubts whether the shares can rise much above 435p, near-term.
But if the bull run in the shares continue, Marshall expects them to test their 1993 peak at 490p.
A long-term chart of BT shows the shares tumbled to 360p in May 1994 from a peak at 490p in December the previous year.
After the usual 38 percent Fibonacci retracement level at 410p, the shares dipped again and spent most of 1996 ranging between 330p and 380p.
But breakout from a bullish double-bottom chart pattern in November 1996 indicated bullish times ahead for BT.

A double-bottom pattern is when a share price tests a support level twice before moving higher. The maximum width of the pattern -- 40p in the case of BT -- when added to the point of breakout gives the next target level.
For BT breakout was at about 380p implying a target price of of 420p.
"But the dynamic trend has not been confirmed by the price relative chart (of BT share price divided by the All-Share index)," said Marshall.
By this he meant that BT's price-relative chart had not yet gone above its previous 1996 peak whereas the share price had well exceeded it.
But one long-term positive sign is that the stock's 200 day moving average has started to curl up after being flat over the second half of 1996, said Marshall.
"There is near-term support at 405p," he added.
-- Pradip Mishra, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7954
